label: accepted

evidence.V1: Front, three-quarter and top views all read immediately as a stone stair flight with side cheek walls; outline symmetric left/right in the front view.
evidence.V2: Big cheek walls and body, medium split treads and copings, but no small tier (no chips, worn nosings, mortar joints); the outer side cheek is one large blank dark panel.
evidence.V3: Clean but primitive proportions: four equal straight steps between two plain wedge walls, little stylised exaggeration (no chunky nosing overhang, no taper or wear).
evidence.V4: Treads and copings have consistent chamfers that catch light, but the cheek-wall bodies and riser blocks show razor-sharp outer edges in the side close-up.
evidence.V5: Studio and flat close-ups clean: no pinches, seams or z-fighting where treads meet risers; A17/A18 pass, 0 flipped faces.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in 3 values (dark body, mid and light treads); sandstone and brick colourways keep the same disciplined structure.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material and stone hue match the modular spec, but the unchamfered cheek-wall edges miss the kit's ~0.05-0.07 stud chamfer on made objects.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default (wedge Part suggested for smooth walking), CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic; T1 tiling along X passes with IoU 1.0.

evidence.V1: Front and top views read clearly as a stair flight with side walls; three-quarter silhouette is a sloped block with coping nubs, still recognisable.
evidence.V2: Side walls with coping (big), four steps (medium), split tread slabs in alternating values (small).
evidence.V3: Stiff: side walls are plain flat wedges and steps are uniform boxes; reads functional rather than confidently stylised.
evidence.V4: Consistent chamfers on tread nosings and coping visible in the steps close-up.
evidence.V5: Steps and side close-ups clean; no seams or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: Stone in three values (dark risers/walls, mid and light treads).
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, chamfered stone treads: kit-consistent.
evidence.V9: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default (wedge Part suggested for walking), CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 pass.

evidence.V1: Front, three-quarter and silhouette all read instantly as a 4-step flight with raised cheek walls; front outline is symmetric about the centre.
evidence.V2: Big (stepped mass + cheeks) and medium (split two-tone tread slabs, sloped cap rail) are clear, but the cheek side faces are large blank dark slabs with no small-scale detail (no coursing, no end blocks).
evidence.V3: Proportions are correct but literal: straight-sided box cheeks, uniform risers and evenly split treads read as stiff primitives with only light stylisation (the inset cap rail is the main shape accent).
evidence.V4: Close_steps studio shows consistent small chamfers on every tread nosing, slab joint and cap-rail edge that catch a highlight line; no razor edges.
evidence.V5: Close-ups (studio and flat) show clean flat treads and riser faces, no pinches, seams or z-fighting despite the 79 deliberate cross-shell overlaps; A17/A18 pass.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in three values (light tread, mid tread, dark riser/cheek); brick and sandstone colourways keep the same value structure.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, chamfers in kit range, stone hue in 3 values per wave-2 modular spec; reads as the same kit as the barrel anchor.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, CanTouch off, Default collision (or wedge for walking), MeshPart white + SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 tiling passes (iou 1.0).

artifacts: large flat unbroken outer cheek-wall face reads as an empty panel

Break up the large flat side walls with block coursing or an inset panel
Add slight variation (worn nosing, uneven tread slabs) to push the stylised feel
Consider shipping the walking wedge collider alongside
Break up the large blank cheek side faces (block coursing, a darker plinth band or an end newel block) to add small-scale detail
